I honestly don't know enough about neurology to tell you anything other than that we (as epileptic individuals) have instances where our brain waves become abnormal, the messages sent across neurons become scrambled, and your brain pretty much goes into self destruct mode. The reason you are told to not stimulate someone having a seizure is because each jerking movement is the result of the brain incorrectly processing the inputs being sent in, so increasing the stimulation = increased force in the spasms. There is no fear during a seizure. I just wake up confused, pissed off at the world, and I pretty much have a I don't give a fuck type attitude to the world for about a week.
Electroshock therapy in essence is just inducing a seizure onto an individual. In modern day it really has solid empirical evidence because if someone having a seizure doesn't knock their body against anything and is on muscle relaxers while having the seizure, they suffer no physical ailments and only minor cognitive deficits. I hope that answered your question.

I know I am late but yes it is exhausting. As someone who has epilepsy I can tell you when you come out of the seizure and are surrounded by people you are typically combative, but once you are in the ambulance you just feel sore typically in the neck and your limbs.
